_comment: Wearly Learning Graph — a directed acyclic graph of concepts a reader must understand to fully grasp the project. Distinct from graph/graph.json (which models wardrobe items + outfits at RUNTIME). This learning graph models the READER's path through the Intelligent Book. Inspired by https://yarmoluk.github.io/Digital-Transformation-with-AI-Spring-2026/learning-graph/ and rendered with vis-network.js. Categories follow Bloom's taxonomy progression (Remember → Understand → Apply → Analyze).

categories.label: Foundation
categories.description: The product problem and the agent stance — the entry concepts every reader needs.

categories.label: Workflow
categories.description: How the agent runs through its seven steps.

categories.label: Knowledge
categories.description: The rule systems and data models the agent reasons over.

categories.label: Personalization
categories.description: Fit profile, wear history, feedback loops — how the agent learns about the user.

categories.label: Framing
categories.description: Body-positive language contract, evidence framing, privacy, ethics.

categories.label: System
categories.description: Architecture, knowledge graph, skill package, the book itself.

concepts.label: The personal styling problem
concepts.summary: The fifteen-minute closet decision: calendar, weather, closet, fit all converge under time pressure.

concepts.label: Agent vs. chatbot
concepts.summary: Wearly reads context FIRST and recommends with a visible reasoning trail — not a free-text response from a prompt.

concepts.label: The honesty contract
concepts.summary: Styling is not an exact science. Wearly says 'tends to work well', never 'is correct'.

concepts.label: Body-positive language contract
concepts.summary: No corrective vocabulary. Forbidden tokens enforced at runtime AND in documentation.

concepts.label: Evidence categories
concepts.summary: Nine source categories every rule traces back to — color harmony, recommender systems, XAI, etc.

concepts.label: The seven-step workflow
concepts.summary: Determine occasion → load profile → check weather → filter wardrobe → build outfit → check gaps → score color.

concepts.label: Occasion classification
concepts.summary: Map free-text or calendar events to the five canonical tags (work/gym/dinner/formal/casual).

concepts.label: Calendar context
concepts.summary: Reads upcoming events; falls back to casual if none.

concepts.label: Weather context
concepts.summary: Live Open-Meteo with seasonal fallback. Temperature drives layering + season.

concepts.label: Wardrobe filtering
concepts.summary: Filter the candidate pool by occasion tags + season + availability + rejection exclusions.

concepts.label: Outfit construction
concepts.summary: Dress vs. separates branching; gym activewear branching; outerwear injection below 60°F.

concepts.label: Wardrobe gap detection
concepts.summary: Compare built outfit against the occasion's required-piece set; surface descriptive (non-promotional) shopping suggestions.

concepts.label: The wardrobe data model
concepts.summary: Clothing / shoes / accessories with type, color, formality, season tags.

concepts.label: Color harmony rules
concepts.summary: Skin-tone palettes (warm olive, cool fair, deep warm) + 0–100 scoring formula (+8 / +4 / −10).

concepts.label: Skin-tone palette
concepts.summary: Three palettes shipped today; design-informed, never claimed as deterministic.

concepts.label: Required pieces by occasion
concepts.summary: Work needs top+bottom; gym needs activewear; formal needs a dress; etc.

concepts.label: Fit profile (user-declared)
concepts.summary: Optional fields: body_shape, modesty_preference, comfort_needs, style_goals, highlight_features, balance_areas.

concepts.label: Body-shape framing
concepts.summary: Body-shape labels are industry heuristic, not scientific taxonomy. Always user-declared, never inferred.

concepts.label: Wear history
concepts.summary: Worn-count + last-worn-date per item, written when user confirms an outfit.

concepts.label: Freshness score (0.4 floor)
concepts.summary: Frequency penalty + recency penalty. Floor 0.4: a much-loved piece is never exiled.

concepts.label: Reject & regenerate
concepts.summary: The agentic moment. User pushes back; agent re-runs with constraints; trail surfaces the rejection reasons.

concepts.label: Favorite stores + wishlist
concepts.summary: Local-only saved retailer hints + saved wishlist items with priority + linked_gap.

concepts.label: The result-dict contract
concepts.summary: Single boundary between agent and UI — steps, recommendation, reasoning, gaps, color_score, weather, event, profile.

concepts.label: Reasoning-graph schema
concepts.summary: Nine entity types + 17 relations modeling the agent's reasoning. NOT the learning graph you're viewing now.

concepts.label: Live-run reasoning graph
concepts.summary: Dynamic graph built per outfit. Same vis-network library, different data.

concepts.label: Skill package
concepts.summary: Conforms to agentskills.io: YAML frontmatter, progressive disclosure, reference files, executable scripts.

concepts.label: Privacy stance
concepts.summary: Minimum-necessary access, no third parties, no implicit data collection. Production roadmap documented.

concepts.label: Before / after delta
concepts.summary: 15 minutes of manual planning → 3 seconds of agent reasoning, with the work made visible.
